 ‘Right Move, But Too Late’: Ex-Vice FM on Indonesian Haze Apology
 Jayanty Nada Shofa 
 November 18, 2026 | 9:18 pm 
 SHARE 
 URL berhasil di salin.
 President Prabowo Subianto sees off Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong after their leaders' retreat at the Halim Perdanakusuma Airport on July 6, 2026. (Photo Courtesy of Presidential Press Bureau) 
 Jakarta. Ex-Vice Foreign Minister Dino Patti Djalal said Wednesday that Indonesia had made the right choice of finally saying sorry for the transboundary haze, but the apology was a little too late.
 At the recent Manila’s ASEAN Summit, President Prabowo Subianto said sorry for the smoke from this year’s wildfires that have caused the air quality in Singapore and Malaysia to free-fall. Speaking to the press in the run-up to the diplomatic festival CIFP 2026, Dino said it was about time that Indonesia apologized.
 “But why did it take [Indonesia] so long? The haze has eased, hasn’t it? There is no dishonor in apologizing. Singaporeans and Malaysians have the right to complain because we would do the same thing if we were them,” Dino said.
 “The apology itself is the right step, but the statement should have come out from the very beginning.”
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Dino — a former envoy to the US — commented on the wording. 
 Prabowo at the time said that the haze was “not our fault”, speaking in front of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart Lawrence Wong. He then repeated his apology before assuring the bloc that “we have done our best”, among others, by placing 104 companies allegedly behind the flames under investigation.
 “If ‘it is not our fault’,  why are there probes into these firms? That means the companies responsible for the haze are within our territory,” Dino said.
 Of all the hundreds of countries out there, the “closest neighbor ASEAN” should be the partner that Indonesia pays most attention to, explained Dino. Within the group, Singapore and Malaysia are the members whose relations Jakarta had to “painstakingly build for years”.
 In a wrap-up interview of the Manila gathering, Wong revealed that he had a “good, candid, and constructive chat” with Prabowo.
 “I will continue to engage him and look forward to working closely to make sure that we can pursue win-win partnerships and collaborations in many different areas,” Wong said, as reported by the Singaporean news channel CNA .
 Massive fire-fighting efforts and rainfall have brought relief to the transboundary pollution.
